    AI Overview
    Tiger Woods has won the Masters Tournament five times. His victories occurred in 1997, 2001, 2002, 2005, and 2019. He is second all-time in Masters wins, trailing only Jack Nicklaus, who has six. 
    • 1997: First Masters win at age 21, breaking the record for youngest champion and winning by a record 12 strokes.
    • 2001: Secured his second title, completing the "Tiger Slam" by holding all four major championship trophies simultaneously.
    • 2002: Won his second consecutive Masters, becoming the third player to repeat as champion.
    • 2005: Won in a playoff against Chris DiMarco.
    • 2019: Captured his fifth title, marking his first major win in 11 years following multiple back surgeries.

    Who has won the Masters most times?
    Jack Nicklaus
    Jack Nicklaus holds the record for the most Masters victories, winning the tournament six times during his career. Nicklaus is also the oldest winner of the Masters: he was 46 years 82 days old when he won in 1986. Nicklaus, Nick Faldo, and Tiger Woods co-hold the record for most consecutive victories with two.
